summary: Children aged 6–7 read and write time to five minutes — including quarter past and quarter to — and draw the clock hands. Two representational hurdles dominate: reading the minute hand in fives (the minute hand on the 5 means 25 past, not 5), and the 'to' side, where times after half past are named in relation to the NEXT hour (although the digital hour stays as the earlier hour, e.g. quarter to 4 = 3:45) and the hour hand sits over halfway toward it. 'Quarter to' is new and easily confused with 'quarter past'. The core teaching moves are counting round the clock in fives and splitting the clock into a 'past' (right) and 'to' (left) side.
misconceptions: Reads the minute-hand number directly (minute hand on 5 → '5 past' not 25 past; on 2 → '2 past' not 10 past)
Confuses quarter past and quarter to
After half past, keeps counting 'past' (35 minutes past) instead of switching to 'to' (25 to)
Names the wrong hour for a 'to' time, or puts the hour hand on a number instead of partway toward the next

activities.title: Count round the clock in fives
steps: Starting at the 12, count the minute marks in fives round the clock, saying the running total at each number: 1→5, 2→10, 3→15, 4→20, 5→25, and so on.
Label (or tap, if using an interactive clock where each number lights its running five-count) each number with its minute value.
Then read a real clock showing 3:25: minute hand on the 5, hour hand between the 3 and the 4 but not yet halfway, so the hour is still 3. State the minutes as twenty-five, not five.
Repeat with other 'past' times to five minutes.
activities.insight: The number the minute hand points to is NOT the number of minutes — each number stands for its multiple of five, so the minute hand on the 5 means 25 minutes, not 5.

activities.title: The 'past' to 'to' switch at the bottom of the clock
steps: Split the clock down the middle: the right-hand side is 'past', the left-hand side is 'to'.
Watch (or move the minute hand) as it travels from twenty-five past across the 6 and up the left side. As it crosses the bottom, start counting the minutes BACK to the next hour instead of forward.
Note that once past the half hour, the named hour becomes the NEXT hour, and the hour hand moves over halfway between the two numbers toward it.
Read twenty-five to four: minute hand on the 7, hour hand over halfway from 3 to 4 — and say why it is 'to four' and not '35 past three'.
activities.insight: After half past, we count the minutes remaining until the NEXT hour and name that next hour; the hour hand sits over halfway between the current and next number to show this.

activities.title: Quarter past versus quarter to, and placing the hour hand
steps: Contrast two clocks: quarter past 9 (minute hand on the 3, hour hand just past the 9) and quarter to 4 (minute hand on the 9, hour hand nearly at the 4).
Say which side of the clock each is on (quarter past = right side; quarter to = left side) and which hour is named.

For a 'to' time, draw the hour hand over halfway toward the next number — NOT resting on a number. For quarter to 4, place the hour hand nearly at the 4; for twenty to four, place the hour hand over halfway from the 3 to the 4 with the minute hand on the 8.
Check: is the hour hand closer to the current number or the next number?
activities.insight: 'Quarter to' and 'quarter past' are different sides of the clock with different named hours; the hour hand moves gradually and, for 'to' times, sits part-way toward the next number rather than on a number.

activities.title: Translate between words, clock face, and digital
steps: Match or build triple sets linking the same time across three forms: words ('quarter past 9'), an analogue clock face, and digital ('9:15').
Given a time in words, draw the hands on a blank clock to show it (e.g. draw twenty to four: minute hand on the 8, hour hand over halfway from 3 to 4).
Given an analogue clock, write the time in both words and digits.
Fill in the digital form of a worded time: 'quarter past 9 = 9:15'.
activities.insight: The same moment in time can be read, spoken, written in words, and written in digits, and the learner can move fluently between all of these forms including drawing the hands themselves.

activities.title: Rehearse saying times aloud
steps: Say target times aloud in words as you point to or build them on a clock, e.g. 'twenty-five past three', 'quarter to four'.
Explain in your own words why a time is 'to' rather than 'past', and which hour you name.
Pair the spoken form with pointing to the hands so speech stays tied to what the hands show.
activities.insight: Putting time-telling into one's own spoken words helps rehearse the relative 'past'/'to' language, but it should stay anchored to reading, writing, and drawing actual clock hands.

checkQuestion: Interpret, then translate. (Interpret) Show a clock at 3:25 — minute hand on 5, hour hand just past 3: 'What time is this? What is each hand telling you?' Then a clock at quarter to 4 — minute hand on 9, hour hand nearly at 4: 'And this one?' (Translate) Blank clock: 'Draw the hands to show twenty to four. Then write quarter past 9 in numbers.'
checkAnswer: Reads 3:25 (twenty-five past three) — minute hand on 5 counted in fives is 25, hour hand just past 3; reads quarter to 4 — minute hand on 9 is 15 minutes to the next hour, hour hand nearly at 4. Draws twenty to four with the minute hand on 8 and the hour hand over halfway from 3 to 4; writes quarter past 9 as 9:15.
